To overcome this, some strategies involve halting DTW early or omitting its computation in advance, tailored to nearest neighbor search scenarios. Nonetheless, PrunedDTW introduced an innovation in DTW's development. Unlike other variations, PrunedDTW does not rely on time or distance constraints, but rather extracts pruned information from the nearest neighbor search framework. Furthermore, it generates optimal sub-schedules during its execution, saving unneeded future computations. We present an early abandoning modification to PrunedDTW, applicable to any query, and also introduce a threshold-based strategy to discard unproductive comparisons. Our experiments demonstrate the enhanced efficiency of PrunedDTW when integrated with early abandoning. We also explore the optimal method for integrating PrunedDTW and early abandoning to achieve the best results in the context of similarity search.

Current educational tools used in the teaching of testing, such as mutation analysis, primarily focus on assessing a student's coding abilities and provide limited insight into the student's understanding of the material. These tools also fail to provide any form of feedback to students. This study aims to address this gap by introducing a new approach: Inquiry-Based Testing. This approach not only evaluates a student's coding skills but also their comprehension of testing concepts, using a collaborative learning environment to facilitate learning by teaching students to design effective test cases. Additionally, the paper includes the results of an empirical investigation conducted on a group of 72 students, which compared the effectiveness of this new approach alongside traditional methods. The outcomes of the inquiry-based testing method revealed higher scores in both practical and theoretical exam categories, as well as improved student attitudes towards the course.

In domains requiring reliability and transparency, explainable AI is increasingly becoming essential for handling the unpredictability of black-box machine learning methods, particularly in healthcare and data protection regulations. However, standard visualizations often fall short due to their inability to differentiate between subtle feature variations or account for the interdependence of missing or abridged features. This issue is particularly pronounced in prediction models that rely on extensive feature sets. Therefore, there is a need for more detailed and precise explanations, highlighting both essential features and their interdependencies. This paper presents a new approach to providing insights into complex machine learning models by integrating an extensive ILP analysis with a comprehensive feature examination. The results show that our method offers a higher level of clarity and accuracy compared to existing standard explanations, enabling a deeper understanding of the inner workings of machine learning models.

Over-smoothing significantly constrains the complexity of Graph Convolutional Networks, making it crucial to understand the root cause. A thorough examination of the over-smoothing phenomenon and Graph Convolutional Networks is presented in this article, including an estimation of the upper limit for its occurrence. The study sheds light on the pivotal elements contributing to over-smoothing and offers empirical evidence validating various countermeasures to mitigate it.

Dark matter particle research has been conducted using a dataset of Z boson candidates accompanied by a significant amount of undetected energy produced by proton-proton collisions. Data was collected between 2016 and 2018 at a facility capable of producing 13 TeV proton energy and had a total exposure of 137.7 fb^-1. By analyzing 79,118 Z boson candidates, researchers observed no evidence of dark matter in various particle configurations, which is consistent with expected standard model behavior. Additionally, upper limits on the likelihood of dark matter interactions have been calculated based on numerous theoretical models of dark matter production.

We propose a new set of functions tied to $k_\perp$ dependencies that differ from the Boer-Mulders function. These functions are connected to quark spin alignment as a collective phenomenon. Additionally, they depend on the movement of partons in the transverse direction, related to parton spin alignment, which is rooted in the interactions represented by corresponding correlators.

Homeomorphisms with compact support on a Tychonoff space can be given several equivalent topological structures by viewing them as either a union of groups of homeomorphisms with the same support size or as a subset of the group of homeomorphisms of its compactified space. A space has the CSHP if these two definitions yield the same topological space, which is the main topic of the paper's methods to prove that product spaces of specific spaces with CSHP possess CSHP.

Research into remote epitaxy on monolayer graphene holds significant promise, enabling the synthesis of highly lattice-mismatched materials and reducing waste from expensive substrate reuse. Nevertheless, concrete examples of graphene-based growth are scarce due to unpredictable interactions with substrate defects. To overcome this challenge, we explored the growth of ferromagnetic Heusler films remote from a graphene template. Through analysis of the out-of-plane and lateral x-z scan profiles, we demonstrated that the growth of these films depends on the balance between kinetic energy and surface energy. When kinetic energy prevails, fast growth rates and smooth films result, whereas increased surface energy leads to slow growth and rough film surfaces. Interestingly, graphenewith pinholes exhibited an optimal growth condition distinct from that with a continuous graphene template. Moreover, an in-depth comparison with van der Waals epitaxy on h-BN/FeTe revealed that the remote epitaxy technique produces higher quality Heusler films. With further investigation, remote epitaxy offers significant potential in producing high-quality ferromagnetic Heusler films.

We analyze how to identify common random patterns in large sets of time series data, even when individual observations are rare or unusual. A new method allows us to make this analysis without knowing whether certain assumptions hold or even what values some important statistics have. By using information about the matrix of average relationships among these time series, we create an estimator of how many common random patterns there are, even in cases with extreme data fluctuations. As sample size increases, the rates of divergence for the matrix's key properties are significantly faster than others. To improve estimation accuracy, we use this information to construct test statistics and implement a procedure for iteratively evaluating whether each key property corresponds to one of these common patterns. A related method can identify the patterns themselves and the study shows this is a consistent approach. To extend the analysis, the study considers more complex scenarios where the components of these time series exhibit varying degrees of independence. A series of numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this new approach. To demonstrate the applicability of this new method, the study includes analyses of prices of raw materials, financial markets data, the relationship between currencies over the long-term, and the behavior of stocks within the same industry.

Recent JWST observations of El Gordo, the massive galaxy cluster, have identified 23 known and 11 previously undiscovered stars within the Voronoi tessellation-based survey, PEARLS. The survey encompasses the entire 0102-4915 cluster, encompassing an area of approximately 7.6 x 10^5 kpc^2. The JWST data were collected in the wavelength range of 0.84 to 2.08 micrometers using the NIRCam and NIRCam Wide-Field Imaging Observations. The team employed a new lens model to determine the positions and distances of the stars. The lens model was developed by combining micro-lensing analysis and macro-lensing analysis to accurately locate and place the stars within the cluster. The results indicate that the positions of 34 stars were determined with an accuracy of less than 0.1 parsecs, both in advance of and behind the cluster. The team discovered a newly identified red supergiant star located approximately 6 billion light-years from Earth, named SMMJ0102-4915e. The JWST data confirm that the star is situated nearly directly at the center of the cluster in the direction of our line of sight. The star's color and brightness characteristics are consistent with a red supergiant star, and its data match existing data for such stars in the cluster. The team analyzed the properties of the stars, including their ages and distribution, and the results indicate that the stars are

Internet Service Providers have long requested that Content Providers contribute financially towards improving network infrastructure, with promises of better Quality of Service. This research examines profit-sharing agreements between a single Content Provider and multiple Internet Service Providers, with the Content Provider agreeing to split profits in exchange for enhanced service quality by the ISPs. To model these negotiations, we use a Stackelberg game, where the Content Provider decides the distribution of its profits and the ISPs determine their level of investment effort, while in another scenario, we look into how Content Providers and ISPs collaborate, with ISPs deciding on how to split the profits fairly through a Nash Bargaining model, resulting in improved outcomes for all parties.

The GNS construction forms a correspondence between abstract collections of physical observables in a C*-algebra and associated physical states. This process essentially amounts to a reverse operation to obtain the algebra given a state. We demonstrate that the GNS construction behaves as a kind of inverse procedure for state representation through an abstract adjoint relationship, capturing fundamental aspects of the algebra's underlying properties.

The $\alpha$-attractor models in inflationary theory hold great promise in the context of upcoming cosmological observations, also having connections to supergravity. Exponential and polynomial models of this type are compared against recent data from the field (notably the 2018 Planck dataset combined with findings from BICEP2 and the Keck array), yielding specific model predictions along with optimal values for associated parameters. The assessment relies on integrated software tools: ModeChord, CosmoMC, and PolyChord, operating in tandem.

In the context of a quasi-Fuchsian hyperbolic three-dimensional manifold with a boundary that approaches infinity, its foliations measured at infinity directly relate to the horizontal measured foliations derived from the uniformization maps associated with its components that extend towards infinity. For a given hyperbolic surface that a pair of measured foliations, denoted by $\mathsf{F}_{+}$ and $\mathsf{F}_{-}$, completely fill, our analysis reveals that when sufficiently small, multiplying both $\mathsf{F}_{+}$ and $\mathsf{F}_{-}$ by a factor of $t>0$ results in unique representations as the foliations measured at infinity for a corresponding quasi-Fuchsian three-dimensional manifold. This new manifold is essentially an extended version of the given surface that approaches an infinite real number. Our finding is similar to another known theorem which asserts that a nearly Fuchsian three-dimensional manifold is uniquely defined based on certain laminations measured along the boundary of its convex core. Our results can also be applied to understand half-pipe geometry.

This study seeks to create advanced mathematical methods and computational tools to model portfolio returns, establishing essential formulas and efficient algorithms using techniques from computational geometry and splines. By leveraging these methods, our approach can efficiently handle an almost infinite number of variables and ensure the accuracy of our results. To demonstrate its practical value, our framework's output is utilized in an analysis of the overall distribution of portfolio yields.

Early detection of heart conditions is crucial, and point-of-care methods like cardiac auscultation are vital for this purpose.  However, accurate abnormality detection from cardiac auscultation sounds is hampered by background noise and the variability of recording devices.  To address this challenge, this study investigates the development of effective methods to analyze cardiac auscultation sounds that have been affected by both types of distortions.  After conducting mathematical analyses of noise effects on feature extraction techniques, the authors propose using a combination of wavelet transformation and convolutional neural networks to improve the accuracy of abnormality detection.  The proposed method is tested on two datasets of cardiac auscultation sounds and shows enhanced performance compared to other existing approaches.

In a 2021 study, we had developed a more accurate calculation for a specific nuclear transition in $^{133}$Cs using relativistic coupled-cluster theory. Recently, Roberts and Ginges raised concerns about a part of this calculation that they disagreed with, but an explanation provided by Wang et al. later showed that their concerns were unwarranted. Despite this resolution, we still found necessary to address a query raised by Roberts and Ginges regarding another component of the calculation. However, our response primarily acknowledges the resolution offered by Wang et al. and expresses gratitude for their efforts.

This work investigates twists on the torus with symmetries corresponding to 2D crystallographic groups. We find that fixing a twist results in a characterizing map for the torus's symmetry group, and consequently, the torus can be fully described by a set of independent twists. Additionally, this research examines how twists are affected by a category of orientation-preserving symmetries, and it relates this to the concept of band representations from the study of 2D topological materials.

Pomona College's Mathematics & Statistics Department has been dedicated to
establishing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all students to
engage in mathematical study. In response to low diversity among majors, the
department initially attempted to address this through targeted programs aimed
at enhancing students' mathematical abilities. Conversely, recent efforts have
shifted to an anti-deficit strategy, which prioritizes modifying the
department's internal culture to foster a more cohesive community. Our
initiatives to boost collaboration, atmosphere, and overall department
climate are detailed below.

We examine the boundedness of the fractional series operator $T_{\gamma}$, with its given function form $(T_{\gamma}b)(j)$, in the context of $H^{p}(\mathbb{Z})$ to $\ell^{q}(\mathbb{Z})$. Furthermore, a counter-example demonstrates that the operator $T_{\gamma}$ does not yield a bounded mapping from $H^{p}(\mathbb{Z})$ to $H^{q}(\mathbb{Z})$.

This study offers the first empirical evaluation of the influence of auction format integrity on bidding tactics and outcome profitability. Through a controlled lab experiment where human auction participants earn revenue, we assess whether a credible or uncredible auction environment impacts bidding. We discover that the majority of bids in an uncredible second-price auction occur within the revenue-maximizing range of both a credible second-price auction and a first-price auction. Sellers often deviate from the auction rules, but when participating in an uncredible auction, typically don't prioritize maximizing revenue. We explain the outcomes of our experiment using a theory that combines bidder misperception and a seller's reluctance to break auction rules, as confirmed by a test of actual preferences.

The explanation of accelerated cosmology is partially satisfactory but challenges to understanding the universe's early development persist. Our research focuses on the promising new theory of $f(Q)$-gravity, which has the potential to address cosmological issues in a more comprehensive way. We investigate the properties of locally rotationally symmetric Bianchi-I spacetime in this theory and derive equations for the density, pressure, and potential energy. Our findings indicate that certain configurations can cause space curvature to increase and ultimately become random, although this theory cannot account for all types of cosmological features.

We initiate a study of local defining ideals of Hessenberg varieties, specifically focusing on regular nilpotent Hessenberg varieties, and their decomposition into vertex-independent components. This research builds on existing findings for their non-degenerate Hessenberg variety counterparts. By leveraging our previous work on the positive Hessenberg variety $H(\mu_0)$, we derive a local defining ideal for the variety's subparameterization defined by $H(\mu)_i$, the subcollection of $H(\mu)$ consisting of Hessenberg functions with support size $i$. Our results encompass both the Grammatico and the de Jong-Scheff forms of these Hessenberg functions. Furthermore, we employ our local defining ideal findings to analyze the Gr\"obner basis for the variety's subparameterization, and employ this analysis to gain insight into Frobenius splittings of $H(\mu)_i$. Additionally, we present computational illustrations of our model.

Neural Painters, utilizing a GAN-based approach, generate brushstrokes that are assembled into paintings. Despite GANs' superiority in AI-generated art, their training can be exceptionally challenging. To address these difficulties and accelerate Neural Painter training, we employed Transfer Learning, achieving a notable time reduction from days to just hours without compromising visual quality. Our findings are presented in this study.

We tackle current, striking discrepancies in flavor anomalies observed within the $K$ and $B$ meson systems, specifically addressing CP-violating Kaon decay and lepton-flavor universality violation in $B$ meson decays, with the introduction of heavy flavorful vector bosons at an energy scale of $\sim 1\,\mathrm{TeV}$. If these vector bosons are substantially heavier, around $\sim 1\,\mathrm{TeV}$ or above, a problem arises, as we then encounter difficulty in resolving the $\epsilon'/\epsilon$ anomaly consistently with the $K^0$-$\overline{K^0}$ mixing constraints. The proposed framework is consistent with the given data within the one-standard-error margin. Furthermore, the proposed model predicts the existence of a $Z'$ boson, which can be detected at upcoming experiments such as Belle-II.

Academic researchers who read research papers usually seek specific information to answer particular questions, but current systems fail to efficiently provide the desired information due to their limited ability to reason complex relationships between paper sections. Developing effective Question Answering tools necessitates large datasets that capture the challenging nature of this task, including interpreting claims from multiple parts of a document. Unlike traditional information-seeking datasets that typically consist of fact-based questions, our proposed QASPER dataset contains a diverse range of questions over 1,585 NLP research papers. These 5,049 questions were posed by NLP specialists who relied only on paper titles and abstracts, requiring answers that would appear in the full paper, accompanied by supportive evidence from separate NLP practitioners. We observed significant performance disparities between existing models and human answerers, with models struggling to consistently provide accurate answers even when combined with traditional extractive approaches. We believe the intricate, often implicit nature of information-seeking questions makes it particularly suited for study.

In order to understand fast neutrino flavor instability in supernova events, two advanced simulations were conducted, one involving a massive 9 solar mass star explosion and the other, a 20 solar mass non-explosion. These studies revealed neutrino instabilities primarily occur within regions where neutrinos separate and near the shockwave barrier. Notably, only the explosive model exhibited the neutrino instability known as the "two-sphere" pattern, attributed to the interaction between neutrinos and nuclear species. This interaction was absent in the non-explosion model. This research found that as the massive star collapses, an inner core forms and causes the neutrino instability to shift towards the core's center. This behavior was not observed in the non-explosion model. Furthermore, by altering mass and angular momentum in the collapsing star, the inner boundary of the neutrino instability was altered. This research suggests that a well-structured star, with sufficient material and rotation, is more likely to experience the fast neutrino flavor instability.

ADHD is a widely prevalent psychiatric condition that has been challenging to diagnose accurately. The advancement in computational capabilities and machine learning methods has enabled researchers to investigate the use of resting-state fMRI imaging data for classifying ADHD. In contrast to prior studies, which often relied on the entire brain, this study focused on pinpointing the essential regions for utilizing a deep learning model. By using rsfMRI data from the ADHD 200 global competition, the researchers employed leave-one-site-out cross-validation to derive an integrated outcome. Notably, the study found that using merely 15 crucial regions of interest for training yielded a 70.6% accuracy rate, surpassing the existing benchmark of 68.6% achieved through utilizing the entire brain. Furthermore, the researchers developed and tested novel models, namely Separate Channel CNN RNN with Attention, Separate Channel dilate CNN RNN with Attention, and Separate Channel CNN slicing RNN with Attention, to identify the most effective architecture. The ASSRNN model emerged as the top performer, attaining a 70.46% accuracy rate with an AUC of 0.72, thereby demonstrating superior performance over existing methods and providing valuable insights for diagnosing ADHD by utilizing brain regions.

In a discrete-time epidemic SISI model where population growth is constant and balanced, the per capita mortality and fertility rates are equivalent, and the model's evolution operator is a nonlinear function of seven parameters. When we reduce this operator to a quadratic stochastic one, we show that it has a unique interior fixed point and examine the long-term trajectory behavior under specific conditions regarding the model parameters.

Acronyms and abbreviations serve as shorter versions of lengthy phrases, commonly found across diverse writing mediums. While they are instrumental in saving space and time in written communication, they also introduce comprehension hurdles if not clearly defined, particularly if the acronym's origin is unclear in lengthy texts. To address this, concerted efforts from both researchers and software developers are directed at creating systems capable of accurately identifying and interpreting acronyms within various contexts. Unfortunately, existing solutions have failed to present a unified, comprehensive approach applicable to different domains and available for public access. In response, our project offers the first publicly accessible, web-based acronym identification and disambiguation platform capable of processing acronyms in scientific, biomedical, and general domains. This system can be accessed via the website http://iq.cs.uoregon.edu:5000 and supplemented with a demo paper demonstrating its utility.

Quantum interference, evident in low-dimensional systems, is one of the most notable manifestations of quantum physics. Historically, quantum interference has been observed in charge transport; however, recent findings indicate that it also significantly affects thermal properties. This insight enables the precise manipulation of heat within microscopic devices through phase-coherence. This study showcases how exploiting phase-coherent electron interference in quantum Hall junctions allows for the realization of exceptional thermoelectric properties and efficient heat rectification. Various heat rectification mechanisms were introduced, including phonon and magnetic field-induced suppression of interference, which fails to account for the observed efficiency. Conversely, we discovered that taking into consideration all possible electron paths results in an extremely high heat rectification capacity. This research presents the current limits of heat rectification and provides a platform for the development of advanced quantum heat engines and devices.

Our proposed DNA-storage system presents a new, flexible structure that establishes a hierarchical relationship among data objects identified by the same primer pair and facilitates efficient data revisions. Unlike existing approaches, in this architecture a pair of twenty base PCR primers no longer defines a singular object, but rather a distinct, independently managed storage segment with its own index. We've discovered that, although there are limited sets of primer pairs compatible with one another, each segment offers essentially limitless internal storage capacity. Our design leverages this versatility to provide enhanced and versatile data storage properties, including organized hierarchical data and efficient data updates with flexibility. Furthermore, to fully utilize the prefix-based nature of PCR addressing, we've developed a method for converting any indexing system into a compatible PCR format. This enables us to utilize primers that can be variably extended to include desired parts of the index, allowing us to precisely locate and retrieve specific data objects within a segment. Our approach includes both a description of the DNA storage architecture and proposed algorithms for data revisions, along with an analysis of the underlying complexities of these processes. We've also performed comprehensive experiments to validate our proposed solution and assessed its practical feasibility. Our results indicate that, although the current scalability of DNA storage is hindered by its lower data transfer rate and higher error rate when compared to traditional storage media, the capacity of DNA storage is sufficient to store a large collection of videos.

Topological insulators represent a significant phenomenon in modern condensed matter research, characterized by exceptional properties of exotic matter states that facilitate unidirectional and unobstructed electron flow and enable precise measurements of the Hall conductivity. Current research has made notable strides in understanding and replicating topological effects through artificial materials, particularly photonic, phononic crystals, metamaterials, and electrical circuits, centered around Dirac/Weyl points. Conversely, topological nodal lines – one-dimensional singularities in momentum space – are relatively understudied. This review aims to illuminate the theoretical basis of topological nodal lines and outline recent developments using artificial materials, featuring examples of non-Abelian charges observed in nodal lines in momentum space and their realizations in photonic systems. Furthermore, it discusses the challenges associated with both experimental and theoretical investigations of topological nodal lines.

In oscillatory media, regions that oscillate faster than their surroundings can give rise to outgoing waves, which are crucial for synchronization across entire systems and are prevalent in many biological and chemical processes. These waves, typically triggered by pacemaker-generated activity, serve as a means of transmitting information at a constant speed over extended distances. This research utilizes advanced analytical tools to explore the determinants of wave velocity, focusing specifically on singular perturbation and phase reduction techniques in the context of two distinct types of oscillators, one built on bistability and the other featuring time delay in negative feedback mechanisms. We examine how temporal separation of oscillatory scales impacts resulting wave speeds and assess the influence of pacemaker size and oscillation frequency. Our analytical findings are further validated by numerical simulations described previously, which were designed to model this phenomenon.

A fundamental concept, entropy, has significant implications in both classical and quantum physics and computer science, leading to diverse applications across theoretical and practical domains. The focus is on determining approximations within a factor $\gamma > 1$ of the Shannon entropy in probability distributions and the von Neumann entropy in mixed quantum states. The key contributions are two algorithms: a quantum one for approximating Shannon entropy that requires $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{\frac{1+\eta}{2\gamma^2}})$ queries, and another for approximating von Neumann entropy that necessitates $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1+\eta}{2\gamma^2}})$ queries. These results hold provided the entropy is bounded away from zero by a quantity linked to $\eta > 0$, and a no-go result indicates the non-existence of polynomial query algorithms for distributions with very low entropy. The analysis considers the most general input model - the quantum purified query access model - enabling handling of both classical distributions and quantum states with full access.

Implementing and deploying effective artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, necessitates substantial datasets for training, testing, and validation processes. Establishing comprehensive data collections, annotated in accordance with standardized protocols, necessitates the setup of imaging biobanks to ensure organized access. Achieving this, however, involves intricate design and careful consideration of technical nuances, particularly data storage and computational infrastructure. Recent advancements creating standardized AI pipelines have simplified the workflow, enabling more streamlined and integrated management of complex data, models, and computational resources. This white paper delves into fundamental technical aspects, offering insights into common challenges and proposing practical solutions for processing and analyzing large biomedical image datasets within an AI pipeline environment.

Physicians' written assessments and explanations of patients' conditions during hospitalization serve as the foundation for official diagnoses as per the International Classification of Diseases (ICD). Current automatic diagnosis coding methods are primarily founded on rule-based techniques that are inflexible and ineffective in the face of unusual cases. To address this, more advanced machine learning approaches are being explored, though they necessitate substantial amounts of labeled data and frequently rely on simplistic disease representations. To bridge these two methodologies and create semi-supervised learning conditions for assigning diagnoses, physicians' written assessments can be utilized to generate synthetic diagnoses based on unsupervised disease representations. This study introduces a novel semi-self-supervised approach, incorporating sequence-to-sequence neural models to achieve this. By jointly optimizing both tasks in a shared latent space that accommodates both synthetic and official diagnoses, we've seen significant improvements in diagnostic accuracy using the 2016 ICD codes. This breakthrough has paved the way for significant increases in efficiency and effectiveness in clinical coding, particularly when combined with simplified differential diagnosis differential diagrams.

Let $R$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables over a field $k$. A monomial ideal $I$ within this ring is considered. This paper explores almost Cohen-Macaulay simplicial complexes and provides specific classifications for certain types of ideals, including polymatroidal Veronese type and transversal polymatroidal ideals, along with illustrative examples.

Due to the diverse applications of machine learning, its ability to identify patterns in datasets is highly valuable, yet the process can be labor-intensive and costly. A major hurdle lies in obtaining extensive training data, particularly for complex tasks. Consequently, researchers have been exploring the possibilities of incorporating artificial intelligence into scientific discoveries. Moreover, as quantum computers have the potential to tackle complex problems beyond their current reach, experts hope to utilize these systems for tackling intricate data analysis tasks. A recent study delves into the possibilities and effectiveness of implementing both supervised and unsupervised learning on quantum systems, using superconducting qubits to simulate two distinct datasets: a quantum system with overlapping peaks and a classical mixture of gaussians. By mapping these datasets onto a binary lattice, researchers were able to accurately distinguish between the two in both cases, especially when sufficient contrast was present. Furthermore, a quantum approach was found to offer an advantage in terms of computing capacity over a classical approach based on support vector machines.

Our analysis encompasses all prime-field microlensing planets from the 2018 dataset provided by the KMTNet AnomalyFinder, revealing 24 total discoveries or recoveries - ten previously unpublished planets with definitive or probable planetary nature: KMT-2018-BLG-2004, OGLE-2018-BLG-1126, and seven other identified planets; combined with four AnomalyFinder-confirmed new planets from published data, and twelve discovered by visual examination. Together, a study detailing sub-prime planet findings is set to complement our findings. Using the method outlined by Hwang et al. (2022), a modification is introduced to their formalism to remove close/wide and inner/outer degeneracies discrepancies.

Differentiable rendering has gained significant attention in image-based inverse problems due to its potential to enhance traditional optimization-based methods and offer self-supervision when combined with generative models. Nonetheless, the existing differentiable renderers have considerable drawbacks when it comes to computing shadows, a crucial element in rendering. To address this limitation, we present an accurate and efficient shadow computation approach that does not rely on approximate assumptions or increased computational burden. Building on this method, we develop a novel system that calculates shadows and uses self-supervised training to contribute to the improvement of differentiable renderers. Furthermore, our system significantly facilitates the resolution of the inverse problem by jointly optimizing illumination, object positions, and shapes. By employing numerical subgradients, our method delivers superior results and substantial reductions in convergence time compared to the existing state-of-the-art methods.

Recent research on transportation networks has highlighted the need to account for uncertainty and reliability by modeling the probability of origin-destination demand and network flow. Building on long-term traffic dynamics analysis, this paper develops a statistical framework to estimate the average and statistical relationship between origin-destination demand and network flow, taking into consideration day-to-day variability. The proposed framework also determines the probability distribution of link and path flow along with their associated costs, and tests the method using simulated data revealed positive outcomes.

In an array of nonlinear oscillators with random frequencies and purely conserved interactions, global phase coherence is demonstrated to occur within finite networks and further examined as it collapses through the generation of localized periodic and chaotic waves following a parameter adjustment. For weak nonlinearity in the system, these global phases exhibit a temporary state of stability, akin to that observed in nearly conservative systems. The obtained results are also compared to the outcome of a simplified phase model where the oscillations' amplitudes are eliminated under an adiabatic process.

The well-documented Aldous-Broder and Wilson algorithms create random spanning trees through random walks, and our analysis shows that combining these methods leads to faster tree generation, particularly when starting with Wilson's algorithm. This hybrid approach can also be applied to enhance existing implementations of both algorithms.

This work presents a comprehensive music dataset named MusicTM-Dataset that enhances cross-modal retrieval capabilities by offering a diverse collection of multimedia data. Currently, large music datasets featuring three modalities are scarce, limiting the ability to learn effective representations for cross-modal applications. To bridge this gap, our research expands on existing musical notation, lyrics, and audio by developing three modalities from previously unknown music pieces by renowned composers. This expansion enables the creation of a massive dataset comprising:

- **Sheet Music**: High-quality musical scores accurately transcribed from iconic scores of famous composers, totaling 106 scores with 1,822 measures.
- **Lyrics**: Accurate translations of sheet music into lyrics, accompanied by detailed metadata.
- **Audio**: Custom-composed audio recordings of professional musicians performing these iconic music pieces.

Our MusicTM-Dataset comprises 1,000 distinct music pieces, offering a vast platform to tackle cross-modal retrieval challenges. It consists of two comprehensive sub-datasets: MusicTM-Dataset-1K and MusicTM-Dataset-10K, differing in the available information about each piece. This dataset will play a pivotal role in addressing the limitation of limited cross-modal datasets, enabling the development of robust representation learning for a wide range of musical data.

## Introduction
Multimedia cross-modal retrieval datasets are abundant, yet representing complex data like musical scores, lyrics, and audio in a unified format is extremely challenging. When two modalities are involved, deep learning can effectively create meaningful representations, but datasets

One major obstacle when working with Linked Data lies in its lack of human comprehensibility, making it difficult for individuals without technical expertise to navigate and understand the data.  Although there are numerous query and visualization tools designed to enhance data comprehension, users often require specialized knowledge to fully utilize them.  In order to make Linked Data more accessible to a broader audience, we develop and present an approach that leverages word embeddings to facilitate visual data exploration within Ontodia and Wikidata.  By training word embeddings on Wikidata concepts and their descriptive properties, we enable users to recognize and understand unfamiliar terms related to domains they are less familiar with.  For instance, training on biomedical Ontodia concepts allows users to visually investigate biomedical relationships within Ontodia while having the option to switch to a domain they are more familiar with.  Our innovative method encompasses two primary modules: a concept embedding module that trains word embeddings on Wikidata domains and a fusion module that integrates these embeddings with the existing Ontodia graph.  Our early results demonstrate the feasibility of our approach and suggest that concept embeddings can be utilized to enhance data exploration by minimizing the cognitive load associated with complex and specialized domains.

We've discovered that in the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with variable refractive index and a defocusing cubic nonlinearity, dark solitons display the same characteristics as in the pure cubic defocusing model. However, adding variable refractive index significantly changes how we assess stability in the dark solitons. Notably, only small and narrow solitons remain stable, with wider solitons losing stability through a resonance mechanism. Furthermore, as the variable refractive index parameter increases, the threshold for these solitons decreases. Despite losing stability, the dark solitons still maintain many of their characteristic features and travel long distances without degradation in models that include random fluctuations and nonlinear losses.

This collaborative approach in visual analytics aims to facilitate seamless interaction between humans and machines, according to various established frameworks. To bridge the gap between theoretical foundations and practical implementation, we introduce an intuitive model for system-assisted guidance and a corresponding library. We present a model for system-supplied guidance based on predefined templates and derived methods. Furthermore, we create the Lotse library, allowing developers to specify guidance strategies using definition files and automatically generate functional code. The Lotse library offers an innovative approach by providing reusable guidance strategies for easily retrofitting existing applications with guidance and promoting the development of generic guidance pattern templates. Through case studies involving VA researchers with different levels of expertise, we demonstrate the library's effectiveness and efficiency. Finally, we outline possible research avenues and present the library's future enhancements as well as the VA research community, serving as a pattern for implementing guidance and enhancing the overall VA process.

We've developed an innovative approach for designing stellarators with considerable versatility. Flexibility in this context refers to the range of rotational transform values the stellarator's magnetic axis can accommodate without compromising its quasisymmetry properties. Our method enhances design flexibility by taking into account coil placement during the modular coil design process, leveraging planar control coils and integrability objectives to minimize the magnetic field's errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by optimizing a coil set inspired by the W7X design, which achieves a substantial reduction in errors and allows for a significant increase in design flexibility. Our research showcases the potential of optimized objects to contribute to the advancement of stellarator physics and engineering.

Achieving uniform temperature distribution within catalytic fixed bed reactors is critical for both optimal production yield and operational stability.  However, obtaining precise temperature readings simultaneously with good spatial and temporal resolution in these systems remains difficult. Our research utilizes the capabilities of real-time MRI imaging in conjunction with the temperature-dependent shift in water's proton resonance frequency to provide precise temperature measurements in a heated fixed bed reactor. The effects of four different heating methods on temperature distributions in the bed and its uniformity are examined in detail. The findings show that the double-sided hot air blowing technique results in the uniformity of temperature within the bed being superior to other methods examined.

Within a cellular environment, proteins and nucleic acids autonomously separate, resulting in the spontaneous formation of membraneless droplets. This process underlies the development of numerous sub-cellular compartments. In a model system designed to understand condensate self-assembly, interactions between a large number of different molecular species were studied and programmed to test for variability and rules. The number of different droplets formed from mixtures increased significantly as the number of different molecular species in the mixtures increased. Most of these droplets consist of droplets typical for the respective individual species' condensates. Moreover, even small changes in the composition of a droplet can cause the exchange of material with the surrounding environment to equalize the composition again. The understanding of the underlying rules of condensate self-assembly could lead to new therapeutic approaches for treating diseases caused by errors in the cellular compartmentisation.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we studied how major sunspots in NOAA AR 11429 rotated in the weeks leading up to a significant solar flare event. Although the sunspots' rotational behaviors initially appeared to be guided by magnetic waves caused by the flare, closer analysis revealed that they were actually moving in the direction the sunspots were rotating, meaning their rotation was naturally occurring. Our research provides more evidence that sunspots are complex, dynamic magnetic structures that cannot be simplified as being composed of uniform, horizontal magnetic field lines.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most relaxed map function class exhibiting a compact, locally oriented structure properties. The concept is equivalent to that of oriented submersions in simple geometric compositions such as colorings, orientability, and compactness. The new theoretical framework enables the application of the b-principle, allowing for the derivation of distinct conclusions in different map function classes through colored submersions, oriented colorings, and orientability, thus yielding a new class of map functions. The primary goal is to demonstrate that oriented colorings in the stable cohomology ring fall within the $\mathfrak{I}$ class, which describes set-defined $\mathfrak{I}$-orientability. The goal is achieved through the derivation of a geometric interpretation for oriented colorings in the stable cohomology ring and the application of the categorical $\mathfrak{I}$-extension functor. The notable outcome of this goal is the confirmation of the Mumford Conjecture.

This research involves comparing the efficiency of Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods for solving complex cardiac mechanics problems on various types of finite element grids. To achieve scalable performance, the solvers employ a Coarse Grid Corneanu-Martin (CGCM) algorithm on the coarse grids. A thorough analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of BDDC and AMG preconditioners on the scalability, flexibility, and adaptability of cardiological simulations using finely resolved meshes, focusing on the balancing factors, mesh partitions, and AMG coarse grid solver sizes.

The ever-growing influence of user-generated content is significantly altering the digital landscape, driven in part by the proliferation of systems supporting content creation, sharing, and management. Among these systems are tag-based platforms that enable users to collaborate in annotating shared items such as images and URLs, leading to user-generated metadata pools and collaborative behavior. To unlock this potential, a comprehensive understanding of current systems is required, which involves characterizing these systems based on usage patterns, the evolution of user-generated content over time, and the underlying social dynamics.

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic wave manipulation, notably in flat acoustic lenses and ultra-high frequency ultrasound imaging. This concept, however, has not yet been implemented at the MHz frequencies common in ultrasound imaging due to difficulties in fabricating complex microstructures. Advances in two-photon polymerization now enable precise manufacture of sub-wavelength structures in this range. However, shrinking structures in size introduces another challenge, where increased thermoviscous effects lead to considerable energy losses, which need to be factored into the design. This work introduces three novel microacoustic metagrating designs capable of refracting normally incident waves by approximately 35 degrees at 2 MHz, utilizing shape optimization techniques and the linearized Navier-Stokes equations. Using two-photon polymerization, we fabricated and experimentally validated microscopic acoustic metamaterials, successfully redirecting incident waves and verifying that a 0.29 wavelength-thick microacoustic metagrating can efficiently allocate 90% of transmitted energy into the -1st diffraction order.

This paper primarily focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the $L^2$ decay rate is given by $\ln^{-l}(e+t)$, with any positive integer $l$. Through the application of the time-weighted energy method, we manage to enhance this rate to $(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{4}}$. Under the condition that the frequencies are sufficiently low, by incorporating the principles of the Littlewood-Paley theory, we find that the solutions have properties belonging to certain Besov spaces of negative order and establish the most favorable $L^2$ decay rate.

Implementing integrated access and backhaul (IAB) through wireless connections offers a promising way to develop flexible and high-density networks. Mobile IAB, which facilitates the connection of UEs in motion, holds potential as a suitable solution. This work takes a different approach from existing literature by providing a comprehensive overview of deploying mobile IAB by covering: the IAB standardization in 5G New Radio (NR); a classification framework for both fixed and mobile IAB; an extensive analysis of mobile IAB performance through simulations; and the open challenges and potential prospects of this technology. The proposed taxonomy organizes existing IAB research by categorizing different perspectives, while categorizing mobile IAB by the type of mobility involved. In terms of performance assessment, the authors analyzed an actual deployment of mobile IAB on a train and evaluated several key performance indicators.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five leading global optimization algorithms as a hyperparameter configuration problem to understand the overall impact of their settings on performance. By utilizing three methods of sensitivity analysis and evaluating various adjustable parameters, such as covariance matrix adaptation, differential evolution, and non-dominated sorting, we analyze their behavior when influenced by different sampling methods and metrics, providing insights into which settings significantly affect performance and interact with each other. The ranking of influential parameters suggests an optimal order of tuning, and our results also shed light on the overall stability of the algorithms.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It subsequently derives a non-radiative condition for particles with arbitrary shapes and temporal dependencies, confirming that the condition is consistent with the Lorentz gauge. The code provided calculates electromagnetic fields for both point charges following lemniscate paths and dipole motions. These field computations enable assessments of the force formalism against standards and help validate assumptions for approximating the dipole approximation. The code is written in Python.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models generally struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and to support this research, new tools are being developed, including carefully crafted evaluation frameworks and benchmark environments. To address this need, we present Lifelong Learning Explorer (L2Explorer), a cutting-edge Unity-based environment that allows for continuous, flexible experimentation in a 3D, immersive exploration setting. L2Explorer is distinct from procedurally generated worlds, which often incorporate randomized components. Instead, we've developed a structured and systematic approach to creating learning curricula in response to controlled changes, along with complementary metrics to assess transfer, performance, and data efficiency. The comprehensive framework and resources provided offer a continuous learning framework with extensive possibilities, and our source code and benchmark settings are accessible via public GitHub repositories.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, will be paired with the Keck All-sky Precision Adaptive-optics system to optimize performance. By covering the wavelength range from 0.81 micrometers to 2.45 micrometers, Liger combines multiple observing modes, offering various spatial scales and fields of view. However, Liger's data complexity necessitates a customized processing system to refine its output in real-time. This processing system, named DRiPS (Data Reduction Processing System), will be entirely software-based and composed of multiple interconnected components. To facilitate communication between Liger's hardware and DRiPS, a series of software interfaces have been devised. We present the detailed design of these interfaces, which include the Liger Software Interface and the DRiPS Interface, as well as the DRiPs Component Model and the testing framework.

This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth travelling waves that arise in the vicinity of the Couette flow in 2D Euler equation, at low regularity in vorticity $H^s$ with $s<3/2$. The velocity of these waves is directly proportional to their distance from the Couette flow. This finding significantly deviates from scenarios involving highly regular solutions in Gevrey spaces, where a damping mechanism prevents large-scale non-linear travelling waves from forming.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it. These modes are selectively occupied by the condensate. Our results reveal a unique method for polarization control with potential applications in spin-based photonics and research on complex optical systems with adjustable coupling properties.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local gradient elements. The specific focus lies within a particular class of nonlocal problems formulated within a given domain in higher dimensions. The formulation is based on an equation where the fractional Laplacian of a variable $u$ is equal to the sum of a nonlinear term that involves the norm of the variable's gradient and an additional parameter with an applied force function. The conditions of existence and non-existence are explored with varying coefficients in a specific mathematical framework and solutions to related problems from earlier works are provided.

The  COVID-19 pandemic, triggered by SARS-CoV-2, has caused the worst global health crisis in decades. As the pandemic spreads globally, effective management depends on timely and accurate detection of the outbreak. Many countries rely on reporting rates, normalized incidence, and time-to-detection to assess case numbers. In the absence of comprehensive testing, these indicators must be relied upon to inform decision-makers. This study compares these indicators, along with other available data features, to monitor the pandemic in South Africa, emphasizing the importance of early detection and consistent data collection.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem generally posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, share a sumset with a size near 2k, then A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions. In this paper, we aim to enhance this by limiting the number of possible summands available from subset B. It's shown that if subsets A and B, of size k, meet the criterion that for every four-element subset of B, the sumset A plus that subset doesn't exceed 2k, it follows that A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions.

In medical contexts, diverse information often arises from various sources, which when combined enables healthcare professionals to form more precise opinions. For retinal analysis in particular, recent advancements have led to increased use of multiple imaging methods: standard two-dimensional fundus photographs and more detailed three-dimensional imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography. Our study employed three distinct multimodal data fusion strategies: 1) a simple, information fusion approach combining two-dimensional and three-dimensional imaging data for classification; 2) a deep learning-based information fusion technique incorporating feature learning and information merging; and 3) a modular information fusion method consisting of independent features learned from different imaging types, merged and input into a classifier. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of fusing multiple information sources over individual, separate analyses.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics with predictive information about patients who are likely to experience severe COVID-19 symptoms.  If accurately identified, these characteristics could enable early intervention and improved survival rates for critically ill patients.  Previous research investigated the relationship between specific imaging characteristics and severe COVID-19 symptoms, but there is still a need to explore additional features and their potential impact on patient outcomes.  This study focuses on potential features of ICU admission that can be detected in X-ray images, and how these characteristics are correlated with life-sustaining interventions, such as mechanical ventilation and cardiopulmonary resuscitation.  Given the scarcity of data, multi-task learning models were trained to predict ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation from chest X-ray images, utilizing two publicly available datasets.  The study validated our approach by comparing it with established baseline models and conducted in-depth analyses to understand the features that affect patient outcomes in the lung and whole-body context.  The findings provide valuable insights into the relationships between ICU admission, image characteristics, and life-sustaining interventions, and set the stage for a broader exploration of the potential features of ICU admission in COVID-19 patients.

We analyze the transmission eigenvalue problem involving $u$ and $v$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with $(\Omega, \sigma, \mathbf{n}^2)$. Considering the case where $\Omega$ is a 2 or 3-dimensional ball, and the functions $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ only depend on the radial distance $r$, we find a sequence of transmission eigenfunctions that tend to concentrate their energies around the boundary of $\Omega$ as the associated wavenumbers $k$ increase without bound. If $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ are constant, we prove the existence of transmission eigenfunctions that become localized around the boundary of $\Omega$. Our results generalize the recent studies in the mentioned literature and also illustrate the influence of medium parameters $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ on the geometric patterns of transmission eigenfunctions via numerical experiments.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities and facilitate its practical use, discovering new intent categories from user inputs is essential but remains understudied. Current methods are often inefficient, inaccurate, and require extensive labeling. We address two key research questions in this area by proposing improvements to pre-training and supervised learning techniques for intent discovery. Firstly, we enhance pre-trained language models' effectiveness in intent discovery tasks by modifying their objectives to account for intent labels. Secondly, we present a new supervised approach that leverages semi-supervised learning with labeled data and utilizes contrastive learning to exploit the inherent structure in unlabeled data for more accurate intent classification. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets reveal that our proposed method outperforms existing techniques in discovering new intents while maintaining high accuracy compared to supervised baselines.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix scheme variables S0,0 and S1,0. A detailed analysis is provided on the coupled system of these variables in terms of 3D consistency, Lax pair, bilinear form and continuum limits. The analysis reveals that the variable S1,0 itself adheres to a 9-point lattice equation and upon continuum limiting, it is related to Lax pair's eigenfunction.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being easily identified due to poor object detection. As a result, low-frequency difficult proposals struggle to contribute effectively. Our proposed framework, Spatially-Aware Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (SABRA), mitigates the impact of false positives in VRD tasks. To counter the imbalance, SABRA incorporates Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (BNPS), which divides proposals into distinct sub-classes based on difficulty and samples a balanced distribution accordingly. To further enhance the low-frequency difficult proposals, SABRA incorporates Spatial Inference, which utilizes easy proposals' confidence maps to indirectly recognize relationships among challenging proposals, without requiring additional parameters. Our approach demonstrates the capability to reduce high false positive rates and show superior performance on the VRD benchmarks VinCE-12, VinCE-19, Charades-STA and Car-STA compared to the current state-of-the-art methods. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/Addressing-VP/VRD_SABRA.

A new measure of quantum correlation between two systems has been proposed, which increases with the weak measurement performed on the first system and uses the L\"{o}wner-Ehrenpreis equation to ensure its indirect measurement on the second system. It can reach a maximum value of 2, and it remains zero only when both systems are in the vacuum state. Furthermore, this measure has been applied to the entanglement correlation of certain quantum states, including coherent and anticoherent states. It has been demonstrated that these states exhibit exactly the same behavior as the well-known Gaussian states. Lastly, a theoretical model has been developed to quantify the quantum correlation cost of weak measurement in optical Qubits.

Artificial intelligence's interest in social networks has been piqued, with applications including personalized content recommendations and social media marketing. Typically, research approaches the complexity of social relationships through multiple variables, such as shared interests, geographic proximity, and personal connections. In this study, we introduce a comprehensive model for creating detailed social relationship maps by focusing on multiple interconnected factors. We develop an efficient neural network architecture to accurately capture high-level relationships among numerous variables and demonstrate its effectiveness on a previously unexplored dataset of social relationships.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding tasks is a crucial goal in computer vision. While CNNs excel in many vision tasks, they have limitations in modelling global, structured relationships due to their localized nature. A potential solution lies in incorporating graph neural networks (GNNs) into vision models to effectively capture these relationships. However, current vision models based on GNNs are primarily static and fail to adequately model long-distance relationships in complex vision tasks. To address this, we introduce a new framework called the dynamic graph message passing unit, which enables models built upon it to effectively capture long-range relationships in vision tasks. It achieves this by modeling interactions between distant nodes in a graph representation of visual data and adapting to the specific requirements of each node's features. This is made possible by a novel message passing mechanism that is computationally efficient and highly flexible. By introducing this new mechanism, our model is capable of scaling to complex vision tasks while still effectively modelling long-range relationships. Our model's capabilities are further enhanced by a new attention mechanism that enables the unit to selectively focus on nodes that are relevant to each target node. This is achieved by calculating the similarity between the target node's features and those of potential source nodes. Our model's features are further enhanced by a new aggregation mechanism that is capable of handling large graphs. This is achieved by weighting the importance of each node group based on their centrality measure. As a result, our model is capable of processing a large number of nodes and effectively modelling long

Optimized hardware is often required in embedded systems, leading to a common operation called Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) over integers. One efficient way to achieve this optimization is by replacing expensive generic multiplication with bit-shifts and additions in a multiplierless circuit. Our work advances the state-of-the-art in optimal MCM approaches based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and introduces a novel hardware cost model. This model counts one-bit adders, demonstrating a strong correlation with the number of LUTs required. Our enhanced model accommodates intermediate precision truncations, enabling significant resource savings when full precision is not essential. Additionally, we incorporate error propagation rules to ensure a specified error margin for MCM results. Our ILP formulation includes these complex constraints, offering significant efficiency improvements over previous methods.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational aspects and core principles of quantum deep learning, highlighting key breakthroughs along the way. It also explores the challenges inherent in quantum deep learning research from multiple viewpoints, followed by a discussion of prospective future directions and practical applications.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be fundamental in 
high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, where significant progress has been 
made over the past decade in advancing the field. This progress could soon lead 
to upgraded existing facilities, enhancements to facilities still under 
construction (such as PIP-II), well-established proposals, or newly emerging 
ideas like the FCC-ee and future proton intensity upgrade at Fermilab, among 
others. Innovations in RF technology not only contribute to HEP but also extend 
beyond to fields such as nuclear physics, basic energy sciences, and other areas, 
as evidenced by European XFEL, LCLS-II and related facilities, or SHINE, 
EIC, and FRIB. Therefore, an extensive R&D program focusing on RF technology 
is needed to tackle challenges in accelerator-based applications and introduce 
new, promising technologies.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, accelerator layout, and detector development for a high-energy Muon Collider as well as the difficulties inherent in the machine and its detector environment.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our results for the tensor mode align with those from numerical simulations, while both hydrodynamic and Minkowski spacetime backgrounds were considered for the scalar and vector modes. It's been observed that the deviations of the relaxation-time-approximation dispersion relations from the linearized fluid limits can serve as a marker for the relevant timescales in the problem.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes could be the source behind the observed excess radiowave signals. By assuming that dark matter exists entirely as these black holes, we calculated that their temperature would be approximately 10^-17 K, resulting in an extremely low heat output per black hole. Due to their minuscule size and redshift since their formation, the universe's radio photons now have an energy that is significantly lower than the EHR (early Hawking radiation) spectrum, with an exponential cutoff at approximately 10^14 Hz. This makes it impractical for EHR to be the source behind the EHR signals observed in 2019, which were attributed to CMB residuals, as the predicted flux from EHR is substantially lower than what was observed. However, we found that the predicted flux from PBBHs (stabilized black holes) is within the range of what was reported in the 2020 experiment by ARCADE6. As a result, the observed signals could be interpreted as the Hawking radiation flux from PBBHs reemerging after the universe's expansion slowed down, which is a natural outcome due to the inflation phenomenon. This is an intriguing hypothesis because the predicted flux from PBBHs falls within the range of what was observed in the 2020 experiment and the signals decay at a rate consistent with what was observed in the 2020 experiment and the PVLVE experiment.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together multi-opcode general-purpose sequential processing with Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to enable Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) at a secure computing offloading level, such as cloud computing. The VSP safeguardingly shelters sensitive data from an attacker while enabling computing parties to obtain secure results after offloading execution at an additional trusted party. A novel five-stage pipeline processor was specifically designed to efficiently process a Secure Floating Point (SeFP) arithmetic operation tailored to the Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) use case, resulting in significant pipeline optimization over prior implementations and a substantial increase in processing speed with area-efficient hardware in mind. Moreover, the VSP integrates a cutting-edge Circular Bootstrapping Approach (CBA) to boost Fully Homomorphic Encryption evaluation speed while minimizing the reliance on Ciphertext Policy Homomorphism (CPH), greatly expanding the processing capacity of Fully Homomorphic Encryption. Comprehensive testing, including benchmarking over Random Number Generation (RNG), highlights the remarkable processing speed and efficiency of the VSP at a secure computing offloading level, surpassing current on-device approximate AI processing benchmarks.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover on graph classes that have limited connectivity.

A previously known condition, based on a certain graph property called "bounded local certifiability," ensured the existence of a PTAS for such problems.

A more recent study reveals that a specific graph property, related to the interaction between a graph and its complement, can replace local certifiability in ensuring a PTAS.

This new property, related to the concept of CSPs being "sparsifiable," has significant implications for approximating CSPs, as it allows the development of a PTAS for naturally sparse problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover, even in the presence of arbitrary valuations.

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactical information, as established in previous studies [Tenney et al., 2019, Jawahar et al., 2019, Hewitt and Manning, 2019]. This research presents two unsupervised constituent parsing models, UPOA and its enhanced version UPIO, both of which use the syntactic distance from the self-attention weights of pre-trained language models to evaluate sentence structures. Furthermore, the paper introduces FP-UA, an unsatisfactory model in the same category that utilizes the full attention weights of pre-trained language models. An experimental comparison on unsupervised and few-shot parsing tasks demonstrates the superiority of the proposed models UPOA and UPIO over currently best-in-class methods. Additionally, the paper explores the effect of head-final word order by incorporating the head-final word order heuristic [Arik et al., 2019] into UPOA and UPIO, as well as FewPU, an unsatisfactory model in the same category that does not utilize head-final word order.

High-definition hyperspectral images possess an extraordinary advantage due to their vast range of spectral data, which far exceeds the capabilities of conventional RGB and depth sensors. Although HSI cameras are becoming increasingly accessible, there has been limited application of their full potential in computer vision tasks. In this work, we explore the capabilities of HSI cameras in a critical computer vision task - semantic segmentation. Given the scarce availability of accurate ground truth labels for large-scale HSI images, we established a novel connection between hyperspectral images and common RGB cameras. We then developed a straightforward yet effective approach to translate affordable RGB segmentation labels into valuable HSI segmentation data. Our proposed hyperspectral segmentation model leverages the rich spectral dimensions in HSI images, and we evaluate its performance extensively using real-world hyperspectral datasets. The results show that HSI-based segmentation surpasses conventional RGB-based methods in accuracy and semantic similarity, and even surpasses fully supervised HSI segmentation model in semantic similarity. Moreover, to validate the practical value of HSI cameras, we gathered a new dataset of affordable hyperspectral cameras - 16 in total, and our results also reveal a notable performance trend.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which presents a challenge to existing angular momentum conservation principles. To understand the underlying dynamics of this star, multiple migration and internal differentiation scenarios were simulated, all of which failed to replicate the observed surface and core rotation rates. Furthermore, our analysis of the constraint parameters reveals that this star does not exhibit sufficient surface chemical disruptions to support the theory of it having interacted with another star as predicted by some internal rotation models.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to be based on the RAM model. Despite this implicit assumption, there hasn't been a thorough examination of the RAM model's basic properties. This paper tackles two fundamental questions: what operations can be performed within a constant amount of time in the RAM model, and what is the least amount of work required to perform a specified operation. We investigate these questions under three distinct scenarios - with a single work unit, a single work unit per bit, and unlimited work units per bit. Our analysis reveals that, even in the most basic scenario, an unlimited amount of work can be performed in the RAM model for a considerable number of operations. Moreover, our results indicate that a detailed calculation formula for the cost of combining unlimited unlimited combinations of arithmetic, comparison, and transfer operations cannot be simplified to a polynomial equation. Finally, our analysis in the scenario where the amount of work per bit is concerned shows that an unexpected combination of operations can be performed more efficiently when compared to another, seemingly related combination. Our surprising findings in the scenario where the amount of work per bit is concerned led us to discover an unexpected limitation in the previously established theorem, resulting in a detailed proof that will likely be useful in other algorithmic contexts.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item in a user's ongoing session, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this innovative method.
